subject: Nazca booby
title: This Seabird Lays Two Eggs but Only Ever Raises One Chick

scenes.text: This seabird lays two eggs. It only ever raises one chick.
Nazca boobies lay the second egg about five days after the first. Even with plenty of food, they keep one chick.
Soon after the younger chick hatches, the older one shoves it.
In about two minutes it's out. The parents don't bring it back.
Why? Up to forty percent of eggs never hatch. It's a backup.
If the first egg fails, the backup lives. If not, it's pushed out. Two eggs, one chick.

description:
Nazca boobies often lay two eggs about five days apart but raise only one chick, even in years with plenty of food.
Within a day or two of the second chick hatching, the older chick pushes it out of the nest, and the parents do not retrieve or feed it. The second egg is insurance, because up to 40 percent of eggs fail to hatch.
What is the harshest family rule in nature?
first_comment: Researchers who kept both chicks alive found fewer mothers came back to breed. Is the backup egg cruel or clever?
